Hide a message in the synonyms of a genome

protein C, 4.175 bits per codonspelling Λ, 1.501 bits

Most amino acids have several codon spellings. BiE chooses among them to carry your text, and the protein stays exactly the same.

Research prototype. The output re-spells coding sequences only; it is not a whole chromosome, and nothing has been tested in a living cell. Identical proteins do not guarantee identical function.

01

Write

Your text is compressed, encrypted and spelled out in real E. coli genes. Press Ctrl + Enter to run.

Use a different genome as the cover

Coding sequences as FASTA. BiE uses its codon law (add-one smoothing) and real genes as cover; the reader needs the same file.

04

Method

How the message gets in, and how much room a genome has.

  1. Compressgzip the text; a novel shrinks to about a third.
  2. EncryptAES-GCM, key stretched with PBKDF2.
  3. Split50-byte blocks of 400 bits each.
  4. Placeeach block picks synonymous codons in 400 real codons.
  5. Readthe same key undoes it; the DNA alone is enough.

The room inside the genome

Entropy per codon splits into what the protein says and the freedom left in its spelling (E = C + Λ).

Each bar: how often an amino acid occurs times its freedom.

05

Verify

Run the checks yourself, in your browser.

1,000 blocks: a new 400-bit payload, key and model cover each time, written as DNA and read back. Every 10th runs twice to confirm identical output.

Specification (BiE/1)

Payload: length (4 bytes), IV (12), AES-GCM of the gzipped text, padded to 50-byte blocks. PBKDF2-SHA256 (200,000 rounds, salt "BiE/1") gives an AES key and a 32-byte stream key; IV = HMAC(stream key, gzip)[0..12]. Block i (400 codons, 400 bits) draws R and V from SHA-256(stream key, i, tag) expanded with sfc32, forms U = payload and V, plus R, mod 1, and decodes it arithmetically through the synonymous law.

Limits. Stealth holds against the genome-wide law only (paper, section 6.4). The default cover is the real E. coli K-12 MG1655 coding sequences (RefSeq GCF_000005845.2); the 1,000-block check uses simulated genes. gzip bytes can differ between browsers; any browser reads any BiE sequence. Method: Theorem 8 of Latitude and Doubt (Atta, 2026). Nothing here has been put into a cell.

The project package (bie-poc.zip) holds the checks and a Python reference implementation that reproduces this page's known-answer fingerprint.
